key_insight: Retaining one fluid relaxation mode is essential to predict nonlinear microbeam response and dynamic pull-in; adding coupled modes cannot replace it.
engineering_relevance: A compact fluid–structure model supports assessment of stable operating ranges and pull-in risk in electrostatic MEMS with squeeze-film damping.
method: Build a reduced-order model from complex modes of the coupled fluid–structure system.
Continue periodic responses in the frequency domain and assess stability using Floquet multipliers.
Map attraction basins, dynamical integrity, and dynamic pull-in using three real unknowns.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against measured and computed microswitch frequency responses, and one fluid mode was necessary and sufficient for all simulated devices.
watch_item: Single-fluid-mode sufficiency is demonstrated for the simulated devices, not universally; strongly coupled films require a correction.
paper_title: Why fluid relaxation modes matter: Nonlinear frequency response, dynamical integrity, and dynamic pull-in of electrostatic microbeams with squeeze-film damping
